cards.text: Friend, earlier in this chapter, Pashhur the priest had Jeremiah the prophet beaten and put in the stocks, then released him the next day (Jeremiah 20:1-3). Here, Jeremiah talks to the LORD, and he does NOT hold back. His first words: "You have deceived me, O LORD, and I was deceived."

cards.question: Jeremiah tells the LORD, "You have overcome me and prevailed." Then he says what his days are like. What does everyone do to him all day long?

cards.text: Every time Jeremiah speaks, he cries out about violence and destruction. Picture your whole job being the guy who stands up in EVERY meeting to say "it's getting worse."

cards.question: True or false: Jeremiah says the word of the LORD has brought him honor all day long.

cards.text: So what if Jeremiah just quits? He tells the LORD what happens if he says he won't mention Him or speak in His name anymore.

cards.question: When Jeremiah tries to stop speaking in the LORD's name, what does he say the LORD's message becomes?

answers.text: A fire burning in his heart

cards.question: True or false: When Jeremiah holds the LORD's message in, he's able to keep it there.

cards.text: Fire shut up in his bones, and he can't hold it in. Friend, I can't keep a surprise party secret for TEN MINUTES, and that's just balloons.
And Jeremiah says he's heard the whispering of many: "Terror is on every side! Report him; let us report him!"

cards.question: Jeremiah says some people are watching for him to fall. Who are they?
The people watching Jeremiah say perhaps he'll be ___, so they can prevail against him and take their vengeance.

cards.text: Then Jeremiah turns on one word: "But the LORD is with me like a fearsome warrior." Friend, in the drawer, my backup was a TWIST TIE.

cards.question: With the LORD with him like a fearsome warrior, what does Jeremiah say will happen to his persecutors?

answers.text: They will stumble and not prevail

cards.text: And their shame won't be the quick kind. Jeremiah says it will be "an everlasting disgrace that will never be forgotten."
Then Jeremiah calls on the LORD of Hosts, the One who examines the righteous. He asks to see His vengeance on his persecutors, because he has committed his cause to Him.

cards.question: Jeremiah calls on the LORD of Hosts, who examines the righteous. True or false: Jeremiah says the LORD sees the heart and mind.
Right after committing his cause to the LORD, what does Jeremiah call out?
Jeremiah says to praise the LORD because He rescues the life of the ___ from the hands of evildoers.

cards.text: Friend, right after that praise, Jeremiah's next words are about one day: the day he was born.

cards.question: True or false: Jeremiah wants the day his mother bore him to be blessed.

cards.text: Right after praise, he curses the day he was born. Friend, the only time I swung that fast was in the drawer: light pours in, I'm SURE I'm going back to work, and somebody just grabs the tape.
He keeps going. He curses the man who brought his father the news that a son was born.

cards.question: When that man told Jeremiah's father a son was born, what did the news bring his father?
Jeremiah wants the man who brought the birth news to be like something. What?

answers.text: A tree planted by the water
A watchman on a high wall

cards.text: He wants that man to hear an outcry in the morning and a battle cry at noon.

cards.question: True or false: Jeremiah curses the man who brought his father the news of his birth because that man did not kill Jeremiah in the womb.
Jeremiah ends with a question about why he came out of the womb. What does he say he came out only to see?

cards.text: And he asks why he came out only "to end my days in shame?" That's where Jeremiah's words stop, friend: honest, raw and right there in the Word.

findings.problem: The card says Jeremiah "tells the LORD" what happens if he stops speaking. In Jeremiah 20:9 he talks about the LORD in the third person ("I will not mention Him or speak any more in His name… His message"), so the text doesn't say who he is talking to in this verse. The card fills in an addressee the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card repeats Jeremiah 20:9 (fire shut up in his bones, can't hold it in) right after cards 6 and 7 already asked about it. It adds nothing new and doesn't move the passage forward. It exists only to carry the joke. The joke should ride on a card that tells part of the passage, such as card 9, or the card should tell the part of verse 9 not yet covered ("I become weary of holding it in").

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: "That's where Jeremiah's words stop" isn't true. Only this lament ends at Jeremiah 20:18. Jeremiah keeps speaking and prophesying in the chapters that follow. The line needs to say that this cry ends here, not that his words stop.

rule.text: Noticing. What he points out must be true.
